enonce_markdown: Given $\mathbf a=2\mathbf i-\mathbf j+3\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf b=\mathbf i+4\mathbf j+\mathbf k$, find $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The scalar product is the sum of products of corresponding components: $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=a_1b_1+a_2b_2+a_3b_3$.

### Solution

$$\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=(2)(1)+(-1)(4)+(3)(1)=2-4+3=1.$$

Treating $-\mathbf j$ as $+1$ gives $9$; a sign slip on the $\mathbf k$ term gives $-5$; reversing the overall sign gives $-1$. **Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown: The vectors $p\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-2\mathbf k$ and $4\mathbf i-\mathbf j+6\mathbf k$ are perpendicular. Find the value of $p$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Two non-zero vectors are perpendicular if and only if their scalar product is $0$.

### Solution

$$(p)(4)+(3)(-1)+(-2)(6)=4p-3-12=4p-15=0\ \Longrightarrow\ p=\frac{15}{4}.$$

The other options come from sign errors in one of the products ($4p+3-12=0$ gives $\tfrac94$, $4p-3+12=0$ gives $-\tfrac94$, $4p+3+12=0$ gives $-\tfrac{15}{4}$). **Answer: d.**

enonce_markdown: Find, to the nearest $0.1^\circ$, the angle between the vectors $\mathbf a=\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+2\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf b=2\mathbf i-3\mathbf j+6\mathbf k$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

$\cos\theta=\dfrac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf a||\mathbf b|}$ for the angle between two vectors placed tail to tail.

### Solution

$\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=2-6+12=8$, $|\mathbf a|=\sqrt{1+4+4}=3$, $|\mathbf b|=\sqrt{4+9+36}=7$.

$$\cos\theta=\frac{8}{21}\ \Longrightarrow\ \theta=67.6^\circ.$$

Using the sine ratio gives $22.4^\circ$; dividing by $|\mathbf a|+|\mathbf b|=10$ gives $36.9^\circ$; taking the supplementary angle gives $112.4^\circ$. **Answer: a.**

enonce_markdown: A parallelogram $OABC$ has $\overrightarrow{OA}=2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-\mathbf k$ and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+2\mathbf k$. Find its area.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The area of a parallelogram with adjacent sides $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ is $|\mathbf a\times\mathbf b|$.

### Solution

$$\mathbf a\times\mathbf b=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\2&1&-1\\1&3&2\end{vmatrix}=(2+3)\mathbf i-(4+1)\mathbf j+(6-1)\mathbf k=5\mathbf i-5\mathbf j+5\mathbf k.$$

$$\text{Area}=\sqrt{25+25+25}=5\sqrt3.$$

The value $3$ is the scalar product $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b$, $2\sqrt{21}=|\mathbf a||\mathbf b|$ ignores the angle, and $15$ adds the components of the cross product instead of finding its magnitude. **Answer: b.**

enonce_markdown: Let $\mathbf v=3\mathbf i+2\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf u=\mathbf i+2\mathbf j-\mathbf k$. Determine a vector of length $1$ that is at right angles to each of $\mathbf u$ and $\mathbf v$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The vector product $\mathbf u\times\mathbf v$ is perpendicular to both $\mathbf u$ and $\mathbf v$. Divide by its magnitude to obtain a unit vector.

### Solution

$$\mathbf u\times\mathbf v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\1&2&-1\\3&0&2\end{vmatrix}=(4-0)\mathbf i-(2+3)\mathbf j+(0-6)\mathbf k=4\mathbf i-5\mathbf j-6\mathbf k.$$

Check: $(4,-5,-6)\cdot(1,2,-1)=4-10+6=0$ and $(4,-5,-6)\cdot(3,0,2)=12-12=0$.

$|\mathbf u\times\mathbf v|=\sqrt{16+25+36}=\sqrt{77}$, so a unit vector is

$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{77}}\left(4\mathbf i-5\mathbf j-6\mathbf k\right),$$

and its negative is equally valid.

enonce_markdown: The points $A$, $B$, $C$ have position vectors $\mathbf p=\mathbf i+2\mathbf j$, $\mathbf q=3\mathbf i-\mathbf j+2\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf r=2\mathbf i+4\mathbf j+5\mathbf k$ respectively, taken from the origin $O$. Find (a) angle $BAC$ to the nearest $0.1^\circ$, (b) the area of triangle $ABC$, (c) the perpendicular distance from $C$ to the line $AB$, to 3 significant figures.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Work with $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$. The angle comes from the scalar product, the triangle area is $\tfrac12|\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}|$, and area $=\tfrac12\times AB\times(\text{height})$ gives the distance from $C$ to $AB$.

### Solution

$\overrightarrow{AB}=2\mathbf i-3\mathbf j+2\mathbf k$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}=\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+5\mathbf k$.

**(a)** $\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{AC}=2-6+10=6$, $|\overrightarrow{AB}|=\sqrt{17}$, $|\overrightarrow{AC}|=\sqrt{30}$.

$$\cos BAC=\frac{6}{\sqrt{17}\sqrt{30}}=\frac{6}{\sqrt{510}}\ \Longrightarrow\ BAC=74.6^\circ.$$

**(b)** $\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=(-15-4)\mathbf i-(10-2)\mathbf j+(4+3)\mathbf k=-19\mathbf i-8\mathbf j+7\mathbf k$, with magnitude $\sqrt{361+64+49}=\sqrt{474}$.

$$\text{Area}=\tfrac12\sqrt{474}\approx10.9\ \text{square units}.$$

(Check: $|\mathbf u|^2|\mathbf v|^2-(\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf v)^2=17\times30-36=474$.)

**(c)** Area $=\tfrac12\times|AB|\times d$, so $d=\dfrac{|\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}|}{|\overrightarrow{AB}|}=\dfrac{\sqrt{474}}{\sqrt{17}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{474}{17}}\approx5.28$.
